ctl.tip: VU meter: smoothed level (RMS, 300 ms feel) with a thin peak tick.
Density meter: the pale bar is the peak, the solid bar is the average level. The gap between them shows how dense (squashed) the sound is.
Input pan: balance of the left and right channel before the compressor. Double-click for centre.
ctl.label: Pan

ctl.tip: Input gain in dB before the compressor. Range -24 to +24 dB. Double-click for 0.
ctl.label: Gain dB

ctl.tip: Number of bands: 1 to 4. Drag the vertical dividers in the graph to place the crossovers. Unused bands are greyed out.

Crossover slope: how steeply the bands are separated, from 6 dB per octave (gentle) to 96 dB per octave (very steep). Default 36. Steeper slopes keep bands cleaner but use more CPU and ring slightly more. Linkwitz-Riley type, so the bands add back flat.

Main Mix: dry against compressed, for parallel ("New York") compression. 100% is fully compressed. 50% is our default: it keeps the punch of the original and adds the weight of the squashed copy. The dry copy is time aligned.
ctl.label: Mix

ctl.tip: Spectrum overlay behind the bands. In + Out shows the input in grey and the output in green. Scale on the right is dBFS.

ctl.tip: Output pan after the bands are mixed. Double-click for centre.

ctl.tip: Output Gain in dB, after the main Mix and before the master limiter, so you can push the sound into the limiter for loudness. Range -24 to +24 dB.
ctl.label: Gain dB

ctl.tip: Master output limiter on or off.
Post limiter gain: a final gain after the master limiter, -12 to +12 dB. Raising it can push the output above the ceiling.
ctl.label: Post

ctl.tip: Master limiter ceiling in dB. Nothing leaves the plugin above this level (the sound is delayed by the lookahead so peaks are caught in time). Range -12 to 0 dB.

ctl.tip: Band Mix: dry against compressed for this band only. 100% is fully compressed.

ctl.tip: Band power: off lets the band pass unprocessed (it still goes through the crossover).

ctl.label: Ratio

ctl.tip: Attack: how fast the compressor reacts when the level goes over the threshold. Slow lets the front of a kick through (punch), fast squashes it. 0.1 ms to 100 ms.
ctl.label: Attack

ctl.tip: Release: how fast the compressor lets go. Below 1 ms it switches to AUTO: the time follows the signal (longer after deep compression). 0.5 ms (AUTO) to 1000 ms.
ctl.label: Release

ctl.tip: Boost: make-up gain after the compressor, 0 to +24 dB. It pushes into the band limiter. With Autogain in System, extra make-up is added for you.

ctl.tip: Band limiter on or off. A lookahead limiter at the end of the band: nothing from this band goes above its Output level.

ctl.tip: Limiter output: the ceiling for this band in dB, -12 to 0. Together with Boost this is how loud the band gets.

other.tip: Test sound for the preview rig.
Load your own audio file for the preview. Nothing is uploaded; it is decoded in this page only.
Sidechain feed for page 2 in Audio mode. Kick track: a separate kick plays the trigger, as if a kick track was routed in. Same signal: the sound itself triggers the pumping.

Preview level (preview only). The factory presets are made for loud, near-mastered material, so the quiet test sounds barely touch them. Quiet: as generated. Loud: up to 6 dB hotter, peaks kept at -1 dB. Mastered: peaks at -0.5 dB, like a finished track. No level ever clips the rig or tickles the master limiter on its own, so 0% Mix is the untouched sound. The Input gain knob of the plugin does the same job on your own music.

Level match (preview only): the compressed sound is turned up or down to the same average loudness as the dry sound, so A/B (B key) compares density, punch and sustain instead of volume. Uses a 0.5 s average. Loops play at 150 BPM; Host Sync and DPC follow that transport.

other.text: Comp vs Dry  RMS +0.5 dB  Crest 9.1 to 10.7 dB  -1.6 LU at e
other.tip: Live comparison of the compressor page against the dry input (after input gain), averaged over about half a second. RMS: average level change in dB. Crest: peak minus RMS, dry then compressed. LU at equal peak: how much louder the compressed sound can be played before its peak reaches the dry peak (dry crest minus compressed crest). Mix, autogain and Level match all show up here.
This strip only exists in the design mockup. The plugin itself has no preview rig.

ctl.tip: Audio: the sidechain signal (after the EQ below) triggers the envelope when it passes the Sens level, like a kick on a sidechain input.
MIDI: each MIDI note-on triggers the envelope. In the preview rig the kick pattern plays the role of the MIDI notes.
Host Sync: the envelope restarts on the beat grid of the host transport (grid and offset below). No audio needed. Our rig runs at 150 BPM.
Trigger sensitivity for Audio mode, 0 to 100%. Higher means a quieter signal triggers (threshold from -6 dBFS at 0% down to -60 dBFS at 100%). Our scale.
ctl.label: Sens

ctl.tip: Host Sync offset: shifts the trigger inside the grid step. 50% on the 1/4 grid gives the classic offbeat pump. Our addition.
ctl.label: Offset

ctl.tip: Digital: the two EQ points are normal peaking filters on the trigger signal. Our interpretation.
Notch: each EQ point cuts a narrow notch instead (its depth follows the gain value). Use it to remove a frequency from the trigger. Our interpretation.
Steep: each EQ point is doubled for twice the dB and a steeper edge. Our interpretation.
Input gain in dB for the trigger signal and the audio. Range -24 to +24 dB.
ctl.label: Input Gain

ctl.tip: Output gain in dB after the ducking. Range -24 to +24 dB.
ctl.label: Output Gain

ctl.tip: Beat grid 1/16: lines and snapping every 1/16 note. In Host Sync it is also the trigger rate (our choice).
Beat grid 1/8.
Beat grid 1/4: one line per beat. In Host Sync the envelope restarts every beat.
Beat grid 1/2: every two beats.
Time shown in the envelope displays. Auto picks the smallest span that fits the envelope. At 150 BPM one beat is 400 ms.

Split frequency between the low band and the high band (Linkwitz-Riley, 24 dB per octave). Everything below is ducked by the Low Envelope, everything above by the High Envelope. Also draggable in the spectrum.
ctl.label: Split Freq

ctl.tip: Hear both bands (normal).
Hear only the low band, to tune its envelope.
Hear only the high band, to tune its envelope.
Level of the low band after ducking, -24 to +6 dB.
ctl.label: Low Vol

ctl.tip: Level of the high band after ducking, -24 to +6 dB.
ctl.label: High Vol

ctl.tip: Strength: how deep the band is ducked at the trigger. 100% goes to silence, 50% to half the level.
ctl.label: Strength

ctl.tip: Attack time: how long the band takes to go down after the trigger. 0 ms is instant (we ramp over a fraction of a millisecond to avoid clicks).
ctl.label: Atk

ctl.tip: Attack curve: bends the attack. Above 0 it ducks quickly at first, below 0 it ducks slowly at first.
ctl.label: Curve Atk

ctl.tip: Hold: how long the band stays fully ducked before it recovers.
ctl.label: Hold

ctl.tip: Release time: how long the band takes to come back to full level.
ctl.label: Rel

ctl.tip: Release curve: bends the recovery. Above 0 it comes back quickly at first and eases in at the end, below 0 it stays down longer and snaps back.
ctl.label: Curve Rel

ctl.label: Freq
